amendment: two additions were made after a first run of scripts/h6_design_1131.py had produced the nine strata, the union and the power tables, and before the final run that the page quotes: the union without the bill stratum (strata.union_without_bill) and the reference rows on all target days (power.reference_all_days). strata.unit: a stratum is a set of target days. Every stratum is read from the calendar at the target day (information-set rule 2). Membership is not exclusive: a day may be in several strata, and 'union' is the set of days in at least one
strata.coupon_settlement: treasury_settlement_coupons > 0 on the target row (#963's, #693's reading)
strata.bill_settlement_large: treasury_settlement_bills > 0 and at least the 75th percentile of the positive bill settlements of the 252 panel rows strictly before the target; the size rule is a stand-in, the threshold is a question for her
strata.month_end_turn: turn_days.turn_label == 'turn': the last business day of a month that is not a quarter's last month and the first business day of the next (#959; the shared definition is #1135's draft and is inert until she merges it)
strata.quarter_end_turn: turn_days.turn_label == 'quarter_end_turn': the last business day of March, June or September and the first business day after it
strata.year_end: turn_days.turn_label == 'year_end': the last business day of December and the first business day of January
strata.quarter_and_year_end: the union of quarter_end_turn and year_end; the testable form of the quarter-end stratum, since each alone is thin
strata.tax_date: turn_days.turn_day_type(day, tax_date) == 'tax_date': the tax_date calendar column on a day that is none of the three turn labels
strata.fomc_meeting: fomc_calendar.fomc_meeting_day == 1 (both days of a two-day meeting), read from the calendar as it stood at the decision instant of the longest lead (h = 5): a meeting not public then is not a member
strata.post_fomc_window: the IORB-change window: the first and second business days after the last day of a meeting visible at the decision instant of the longest lead. A change in IORB takes effect on the first of them, and it is announced only at the meeting, so a realized change cannot define membership; the window is the scheduled calendar's. Whether the realized changes fall in it is reported, ex post
strata.union_without_bill: the union without bill_settlement_large: the days in at least one of the other strata
strata.thin: a stratum with fewer than minimum_events target days in the history is counted and not powered on its own

series.days: decision days from 2020-04-03 whose fifth target is on or before 2025-12-31, on the days B1, B2, B1', the calendar benchmark and spread_mr_ctx all have a forecast, built by scripts/b1_calendar_960.py's build_frame unchanged; lockbox.require_unlocked on every decision and target day
series.target_score: the mean over leads 1-5 of the cell scores that target the day, kept only where all five cells exist (scripts/contiguous_calibration_963.py's target_scores)
series.metrics: grid CRPS (the primary score) and upper-tail twCRPS (the key secondary)
series.d: d_e = S(benchmark) - S(candidate) on the target day e of a stratum, in date order, positive favours the candidate

benchmarks.calendar: repo_model.risk_date_spread.calendar_forecast (#693): the trailing year's spreads of the target's risk type. It is defined at a lead only where the target is a quarter-end, month-end (last two business days), tax date or announced coupon settlement; a target day with a calendar forecast at fewer than five leads is left out of its leg, and the stratum's covered count is reported

power.method: #963's contiguous windows, in events: for a stratum's d series of n events, every window of N consecutive events (none wrapping); a window's statistic is its mean over its Newey-West standard error at lag 3 (scoring_protocol._standard_error, hac_lag 3, the lag #963 uses between events), relative to the series' mean. c is the 0.95 quantile of those statistics on the centred series: the value at which the bound covers 95% of windows
power.alternative: power at skill s is the share of contiguous windows whose statistic plus s * mean(S(benchmark) on the stratum) over the window's standard error exceeds c: the windows' own dependence and variance, a mean shifted to skill s
power.window_events: N = round(window_years * events per year of the stratum), events per year being n over the years from the first to the last event; at least the lag + 2
power.effective_windows: n / N, the windows the series holds without overlap; windows of a persistent series overlap in information, so it is an upper count of independent ones
power.size: the share of the null windows above the normal one-sided 95% value 1.6448536269514722
power.union_series: the union's events in date order, one d per target day
power.reference_all_days: H5's own unit on the same history: every target day of the series in date order, d against B1, B1' and B2, windows of 1, 2 and 3 years of target days (N = round(years * target days per year)), the protocol's Newey-West lag 10 (scoring_protocol.HAC_LAG), the same c, size and power. It is a reference row, not a stratum

reading_rules.design_rule: none is declared. The page reports c, size and power per stratum and window; which stratum is the unit of evidence, the window, the multiplicity treatment and the MME are the questions it lists with a default for her
reading_rules.thin: a stratum below minimum_events is counted and not powered; the union and the quarter_and_year_end form stand in for it

limits: no published record, declaration or critical value changes; the protocol's constants are only read. The series are one candidate's proxy against four benchmarks on one history; a quantile of contiguous windows rests on a handful of independent stretches, which the effective-window count states. The settlement flags and IORB window are read as the panel and the FOMC calendar hold them, not re-dated per lead beyond what is stated above
